review_role: Post-hoc candidate feasibility on exposed development inputs; not a performance experiment

items.scope: Existing v2 Native/App Web named-hardware-family relation
items.reason: Every Native renderer contains SwiftShader; software rendering is excluded from this hardware-family relation.
items.additional_boundary: The existing family list is adreno/mali/powervr/tegra/vivante. NVIDIA in the Web attack string is not a recognized family in this parser. Do not turn unknown into a mismatch or extend the list only to match this attack.
items.next_requirement: Evidence with comparable named hardware families and justified parser coverage; current all-software data cannot evaluate that hypothesis. Physical-path identity is NOT a v2 prerequisite for limited research risk.

items.reason: Software exclusion makes the existing relation inapplicable here. Independently, v2 does not give this backend marker a risk role, even on synthetic non-software inputs.
items.next_requirement: Do not remove the software gate to obtain an apparent detection gain. A new research hypothesis would require separately justified semantics and benign rendering-path controls.

items.scope: Raw string comparison only; not registered for selection
items.reason: Native GLES and WebGL use separate contexts and may use different drivers or wrappers. Same-family Adreno and ANGLE-wrapped Adreno are a tested counterexample to treating exact spelling inequality as a hardware conflict.
items.next_requirement: Semantic normalization and legitimate path controls; exact equality on current software baselines is not a general invariant.

items.reason: The changed vendor and renderer both report NVIDIA. The vendor field can identify a driver supplier or wrapper rather than the hardware family; no validated naming-equivalence parser was introduced or evaluated.
items.next_requirement: Define meaningful comparable tokens and unknown states from broader benign implementations before considering a rule.

items.scope: Extension count, texture size, viewport limits and line-width range
items.reason: These fields do not change in any of the 126 graphics triplets. Extension count distinguishes API/WebView environments, not the WebGL intervention within an environment.
items.next_requirement: Do not learn an environment identifier as evidence that the renderer intervention occurred.

items.reason: The probe creates WebGL1 before requesting WebGL2 on the same canvas. Desktop browser reproduction shows false on the reused canvas and true on a fresh canvas.
items.next_requirement: Version a separate-canvas collector fix and validate it. Do not rewrite historical flags or infer Android WebGL2 capability from the desktop reproduction.

items.scope: Pre/intervention/post sequence, a different input task
items.reason: Paired transitions establish observed intervention effects in this controlled study. A deployed single observation does not have a trusted clean reference or future clean_post.
items.next_requirement: A separately declared temporal-reference task and benign configuration-change controls; never use phase labels or clean_post as present-time detector features.
